content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim against the evidence, starting with the root cause: a code change on io-shop stopped each shopper's saved spending-this-month figure from updating on purchase. The second claim is that shoppers saw no errors, yet anyone who bought after the change had totals that no longer matched their actual purchases, since current-month purchases written afterwards left the total short.

I'm going through the remaining claims one by one: the Argus rollback decision, the recommendation to roll io-shop back, the draft fix PR #555, and the point that none of the fix's changes have run yet. Each of these lines up with the evidence I have, so I'm treating them as supported.

supported.quote: A code change on io-shop stopped the shop from updating each shopper's saved spending-this-month figure when they bought something.
rows: Why, in plain words: A code change stopped the shop from updating

supported.quote: Shoppers saw no errors, but for shoppers who made purchases after the change, the saved monthly spend totals stopped matching what they had actually bought.
rows: What a reader saw: Shoppers saw no failure

supported.quote: This matters because the parts of the shop that show and check that figure still read the saved copy.
The problem has gone on for {duration}.
rows: How long it lasted: at least 7d 0h 0m 32s {duration}

rows: What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none so far {customer_loss}

Instead, it recommends rolling io-shop back.
